In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of the silicon and the germanium analogues (L(Dip)M=E(=S)OML(Dep)) of the respective thiobenzoic acids (M=Si, Ge).
the development of new synthetic methods and the characterization of novel compounds of main group elements with transition-metal centers.
the synthesis and characterization of the silicon and the germanium analogues to thiocarboxilic acids and their metal complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mn(II) nacnac complexes [(L(Dep))Mn(2)(μ-X)(2)] (X=Br, 2, μ-H, 3) are versatile reagents to access new manganese(II) compounds with different ligand environments.
the E=S double bond in 4 and 6 is stabilized by both the E-S-Mn and E-O-Mn interaction, which leads to an increase in the Mn-S bond length and an increase in the S-Mn-S angle.
the heavier thiocarbothioate anions are more stable than the corresponding thiocarboxylation anions, which is in contrast to the lighter thiocarboxyla- tion anion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mn nacnacs are very good reagents to prepare heavier thiocarboylate complexes.
the heavier thiocarbylates [L(Dip)(Si, Ge)(=S)(OR)] (R=H, Me) can be regarded as heavier thiocarbons, and the corresponding transition-metal complexes as heavier thioformyls.
manganese(II) nacnac complexes can act as a versatile reagent for the synthesis of a variety of new heavier thiocarbylates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Si=S and the Ge=S functionalities can be used as a versatile platform for the preparation of new organosilicon and organogermanium complexes, and that the Si=S double bond is a suitable functional group for further metalation reactions.
the Si=S and the Ge=S bonds are more stable than the C=S bonds in the corresponding carboxylate analogs.
the heavier thiocarbylate ligands are able to stabilize a manganese hydride species, which is not accessible with the lighter thiocarbylates.
